findings.title: Standalone B>1 catalog speedup is not a fair hardware advantage
findings.detail: Catalog speedup versus its own B1 point reaches 1.704x/2.631x/3.595x, but strong zero receives the same B accumulator banks and update ports and reaches 1.994x/3.962x/7.598x. The fair equal-B catalog/zero ratio strictly falls from 1.435 at B1 to 1.227/0.953/0.679. B4 and B8 are already slower than equal-B zero.

findings.title: B-way destination resources are unpriced
findings.detail: B requires independent destination accumulator banks/update ports, gather/list storage, and broadcast/crossbar. No matched DC/PTPX or physical SRAM/interconnect result exists. This blocks resource-normalized performance even if the trace cycles had improved fairly; here the equal-B result already closes the direction without needing that missing evidence.

findings.title: Throughput divided by B is diagnostic, not throughput per area
findings.detail: The 0.852/0.658/0.449 proxy pessimistically treats total cost as proportional to B, although fixed logic and storage exist. It is not sufficient alone for NO-GO and must not be quoted as physical throughput/area. The NO-GO instead follows from monotonically degrading equal-B advantage even when added resources are treated as free.

findings.title: Payload exact-once wording must remain run-scoped
findings.detail: M458 itself has a valid marker and 80-file exact-once audit. Independent M459 R1 and the two fail-closed technical recovery contracts each authorized their own read-only pass; R1/R2 are preserved DO_NOT_CITE and only R3 is admitted. The inherited machine-result field saying 'second_pass' is a stale label, not a claim that the entire review history read payloads only once.

allowed_claim: On the frozen four-Conv trace, exact destination multicast is mathematically valid, but when strong zero receives the same B destination banks/update ports the catalog advantage strictly degrades for B=2/4/8; therefore B>1 RTL is closed.
